thread:
anne (PM): Quick intake — trying to capture the problem + acceptance for the quantized model rollout guardrails. Posting a rough PRD skeleton, want engineering/security/metrics + design takes before EOD.

Problem: some enterprise customers want lower-cost inference via int8/4 quantized variants but are worried about hallucinations and latency variance. We need a safe rollout path that: reduces cost by ~20-40% on steady workloads, preserves customer-visible quality within an acceptable delta, and can automatically fall back without customer disruption.

Goals:
- Define rollout criteria (per-tenant & global) for enabling quantized variants.
- Specify measurable quality thresholds and observability hooks.
- Implement automatic fallback paths (route to FP32 / higher-precision copies) with minimal user impact.
- Provide Dashboard + alerts for regressions.

Non-goals:
- Not aiming to re-train or fine-tune models to fix quantization drift.
- Not a general-purpose model selection UI in this phase.

Success metrics (proposal):
- Cost reduction: % tokens cost decrease per tenant (target: 20% median for eligible tenants).
- Quality: downstream task pass-rate delta <= 2 percentage points on tenant eval-suite.
- Latency: p95 latency increase <= 10ms or within agreed SLA.
- Rollback rate: auto-fallback triggers < 0.5% of requests per day (target).

Acceptance criteria (draft):
1) There exists a canary path: 1-5% traffic to quantized variant per-tenant with tracing enabled.
2) Per-tenant eval harness runs daily against owner-provided prompts; difference vs baseline measured.
3) If metric breach occurs (quality delta > 2pp OR latency p95 > SLA), requests are transparently routed to baseline model and an alert is raised.
4) Dashboard surfaces per-tenant % cost savings, quality delta, and fallback counts.
5) Rollout config supports: min_traffic_pct, max_traffic_pct, quality_thresholds, and fallback_model.

Edge cases / questions for engineering:
- raj (Eng): How feasible is per-tenant prefix KV cache invalidation when switching routes? Are there cost/latency spikes during switch?
- raj (Eng): Also need to confirm sampling strategy for online evals — we should avoid skewing production billing.

Proposed rollout mechanics (proto):
- Step 0: Owner opt-in and upload of eval prompts (or select from templates).
- Step 1: Canary 1% traffic for 24h -> run automated evals + observe.
- Step 2: Gradual increase to 25% over 72h if metrics OK.
- Step 3: Optional tenant-level full enable.
- Fallback: immediate routing to fallback_model with retry-after header to minimize client-side errors.

Open implementation questions (please chime in):
- lisa (Data): what minimum sample size for canary evals gives acceptable confidence for 2pp threshold?
- tom (Design): UX for tenants when we’ve auto-failed them — do they see a banner, or just an annotated metric?
- raj (Eng): cost accounting — how do we report savings when some traffic still goes to FP32?

Replies:

raj (Eng): Mostly doable. KV invalidation is the tricky part; switching to a new model variant will make the KV cache incompatible. Options: one-shot warmup (serve cold until filled) or maintain separate caches per variant (we'll pay memory). Warmup causes tail latency initially.

lisa (Data): For binary pass/fail task suites, with target delta 2pp, we need ~2000 paired samples per tenant to get decent power if base rate ~80%. For chatty open prompts it's noisier — suggest combining daily sample + rolling 7d aggregation. Also recommend A/B hypothesis testing with false discovery control across tenants.

tom (Design): UX suggestion: show a non-blocking banner in Console when tenant-level fallback occurs + a changelog row for the model routing decision. For critical apps, let tenant opt to receive an email on auto-fallback.

raj (Eng): Sampling: we'll use 1-in-N request sampling for deep evals and keep a separate evaluation pool to avoid billing surprises. Counters/metrics tagged with tenant + variant.

anne (PM): Good — can we agree on the acceptance checklist by tomorrow? Quick asks: raj please call out KV strategy and plumb metrics IDs; lisa please propose exact statistical test & min sample size; tom please mock the banner + dashboard widget.

oncall-bot: NOTE: If auto-fallback triggers > 1000/day across system, incident runbook "quant-rollout-regression" will fire. Link: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/quant-rollout-regression

raj (Eng): I'll write a short RFC for cache strategy + switch plan and link monitoring metric names: rwd.quant.fallback.count, rwd.quant.quality.delta, rwd.quant.cost.savings. Expect draft by EOD tomorrow.

lisa (Data): I'll surface a small script to simulate tenant-level power for different base rates. Will include recommended rolling window and FDR approach.

tom (Design): Mockups will be in Figma under /product/quant-rollout > screens v1. ETA: 48h.

anne (PM): Thanks all — if no major objections I’ll convert this to a formal PRD section and assign owners. Please drop any hard blocks in this thread. :thumbsup:"
